# bugs #2733: Warning 158 for constant left shifts and sums whose value fits in the unsigned char that is assigned

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2733/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Confirm the decision of bug #3986, apply its patch after the patch for local 0013, and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3986.patch](../../patches/bugs-3986.patch), commit [`f955bae8b`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/f955bae8b9ad37f7d01b4a986ef980754f154ce4). Apply after `local-0013.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228 for mcs51, `unsigned char c = 1 << 7;` in a function and the assignment `c = 1 << 7;`
get warning 158, "overflow in implicit constant conversion", and the value 128 fits. Both were
compiled in the small, medium, large, and huge models, and with `--stack-auto` in the small and
large models, and both get the warning each time. At file scope the declaration gets it in the
large and huge models only. In the `main.c` attached to the sixth comment, the declaration with
`0x80 | 0x00 | (0x01 << 2)` gets the warning in each of these six combinations, and the two other
declarations compile without it. The byte that the code stores is correct.

The statements of the second comment compile on r17228 without a message: `1u << 15` for an
unsigned int, and `1ul << 31` and `1ull << 31` for an unsigned long, at file scope, in a
function, and as an assignment. The revision that removed that warning was not identified.

The fourth comment links a forum thread about constant sums. On r17228, `1 + 0x80` gets the
warning as an element of a const unsigned char array and in an assignment to an unsigned char.

## Cause

The entry for bug #3986 describes the cause. When a value is assigned to a char, `decorateType` in
`src/SDCCast.c` casts the literal operands of `+`, `-`, and `<<` to char before the constant is
computed, and an int literal becomes a signed char. `1 << 7` becomes -128, and `checkTypes` in
`src/SDCCicode.c` reports that value for the unsigned char. In the fifth comment a maintainer
names the propagation of `RESULT_TYPE_CHAR` as the cause.

In the expression of the sixth comment, `0x01 << 2` becomes the signed char constant 4, and
`0x80 | 0x00` is the unsigned char constant 128. `valBitwise` in `src/SDCCval.c` computes `|` of
an unsigned char constant and a signed char constant in signed char, and the result is -124.

## Fix

The patch for bug #3986 fixes this ticket, and another change is not needed. `decorateType`
applies the integer promotions to two literal operands of `+`, `-`, and `<<` when the result type
is char. `1 << 7` is 128, and `0x01 << 2` is 4, which `cheapestVal` makes an unsigned char.

## Decision

The patch also adds warning 158 to constant sums, differences, and left shifts whose value does
not fit, such as `s = 1 << 7` for a signed char `s`. The entry for bug #3986 has the choices that
a maintainer should confirm.

## Verification

The statements under Finding were compiled for mcs51 by r17228 and by r17228 with the patches of
this report, in the six combinations of model and `--stack-auto` under Finding. With the patches
the compiler does not print a message for them, and its assembly is equal to the assembly of
r17228. r17228 with the patch for bug #3986 and without the other patches was not built, and
other ports were not tested. `support/valdiag/tests/bug-3986.c`, the test of the patch, has
`u = 1 << 7` and the call `g (1 << 7)`. It does not have the expression of the sixth comment.

## Related

- Bugs #2877 and #3094 report this cause for constant sums.
- The fault of `valBitwise` remains with the patch, and the entry for bug #3986 lists it.
  `unsigned char a = (unsigned char) 0x80 | (signed char) 4;` gets warning 158 with the patches.
- At file scope, `printIvalType` in `src/SDCCglue.c` reports the warning for initializers that
  are emitted as data, which objects in xdata and const objects have. It calls `werror`, which
  takes the line from the global `lineno`. In the large and huge models, `unsigned char a = 300;`
  gets warning 158 twice on r17228 and with the patches, and the second message has the line of
  the last declaration with an initializer at file scope. This is not fixed.
